title: Days and dates
summary: Sequence days and months and begin recording time.
subject: maths

difficultyRamp.within: Q1 fills a gap before Wednesday. Q2 orders days across a week boundary. Q3 finds the weekend. Q4 counts months in a year. Q5 fills a gap after April. Q6 orders four months. Q7 crosses into a new year. Q8 compares units to a minute. Q9 orders units. Q10 chooses a unit for reading time.
difficultyRamp.versus: Easy uses pictures for parts of the day, a week strip and a calendar date. Medium uses before and after across week and month boundaries. Hard works backwards from yesterday, moves two months across a year boundary and reads named time records.

questions.prompt: What day comes just before Wednesday?
questions.explanation: Tuesday comes before Wednesday. Thursday comes after it.

narration.prompt: What day comes just before Wednesday?

questions.prompt: Tap the days in order, starting with Friday.
questions.explanation: After Sunday, a new week starts with Monday.

narration.prompt: Tap the days in order, starting with Friday.

questions.prompt: Tap the two days at the weekend.
questions.explanation: Saturday and Sunday make the weekend.

narration.prompt: Tap the two days at the weekend.

questions.prompt: How many months are in one year?
questions.explanation: A year has twelve months, from January to December.

narration.prompt: How many months are in one year?

questions.prompt: What month comes just after April?
questions.explanation: May follows April. March comes before April.

narration.prompt: What month comes just after April?

questions.prompt: Tap the months in order, starting with April.
questions.explanation: April is followed by May, June and July.

narration.prompt: Tap the months in order, starting with April.

questions.prompt: What month comes just after December?
questions.explanation: January follows December at the start of a new year.

narration.prompt: What month comes just after December?

questions.prompt: Tap the two units longer than one minute.
questions.explanation: An hour and a day each last longer than one minute.

narration.prompt: Tap the two units longer than one minute.

questions.prompt: Put these lengths of time in order, from shortest to longest.
questions.explanation: Seconds are shorter than minutes. Minutes are shorter than hours. Hours are shorter than days.

narration.prompt: Put these lengths of time in order, from shortest to longest.

questions.prompt: Sam reads a book. What could we use to time it?
questions.explanation: Minutes suit a reading session. Seconds are very short, while months and years are much longer.

narration.prompt: Sam reads a book. What could we use to time it?
